buyer_test_question: Would CereVasc pay to license or acquire this invention?
buyer_test_rationale: CereVasc's current eShunt has no continuous patency monitoring. 15-20% of shunts fail due to occlusion; current detection is post-symptomatic. This invention would: (1) differentiate eShunt from competitors by adding continuous monitoring, (2) reduce revision surgeries (cost savings for payers), (3) generate monitoring data that could support future regulatory claims. However, the 103 obviousness uncertainty over EP3212275A1 and the evidence gaps (41 foreign patents unaudited) require resolution before acquisition.
strategic_value: HIGH — monitoring is the #1 unmet need in CSF shunt management
buyer_objections: 103 obviousness risk over EP3212275A1 (CereVasc's own prior art)
Added manufacturing cost ($50-80/unit) vs. eShunt base cost
milestones_for_buyer_ready: Patent counsel opinion on 103 obviousness over EP3212275A1
Claim-level search of 90,264 implantable pressure sensor patents for L4-L6 combination
In vivo proof-of-concept (swine — confirm CSF-venous differential is measurable)
IDE submission for pivotal clinical trial
